steps.title: Jehoiakim vassalized
steps.text: Daniel and the royal youths deported.
steps.detail: Carchemish is the year Babylon breaks Egypt's hold on the coast, and Jerusalem changes hands as a vassal. The first group taken is the one the book follows: royal youth chosen for the court school. Daniel's exile begins here, not in 586.

steps.title: Jehoiachin deposed
steps.detail: Jehoiakim's rebellion brings the army back. The young king is carried off with the craftsmen and smiths, and a prophet of the exile goes with them: Ezekiel dates his own call to the fifth year of that captivity among the captives by the river of Chebar. The city still stands.

steps.title: Zedekiah blinded
steps.detail: The last siege ends with the house of the LORD burned and the walls broken down. Zedekiah flees toward the Jordan, is taken, and is blinded after watching his sons killed. Three campaigns, three separate dates: the book's first verse sits at the first of them.
